assessments.reasoning: The Input Functions section defines read as consuming one textual expression and producing a Lisp object. Introduction to Evaluation states that reading and evaluation are separable and leaves the decision of evaluating the returned object to the caller.

challenge.method: Consider an input stream containing two forms and an unterminated form. Compare an object used as data with a load operation that reads then evaluates forms. Check the source distinction between syntax, object and evaluator.
challenge.results: Success returns the object of the first expression and does not itself evaluate it. The EOF path is separate. A loader or caller choosing evaluation is an additional operation.

limitations: The claim does not establish that arbitrary reading is side-effect-free or that this is how any byte-code or native-code loader handles its representation.
